content_sections.heading: About JU
content_sections.text: Shabdakalpa is being executed by the School of Cultural Texts and Records, Jadavpur University. Its Project Co-ordinator is Professor Sukanta Chaudhuri, Professor Emeritus, Jadavpur University.

content_sections.heading: JU Project Fellow Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Master's degree with minimum 55% marks (grade B+), preferably in a Humanities discipline, Computer Science, Computer Applications or Information Technology. Master's degree holders in other disciplines may be considered if found suitable in other respects. Experience of computer operation in projects involving textual computing, computational linguistics, natural language processing or other relevant field. Command of the Bengali language, spoken and written, at first-language level, with knowledge of Bengali grammar and ability to interpret and analyse Bengali texts. Skill in operating the Bengali keyboard with Avro keyboard software. Master's degree with minimum 55% marks in Sanskrit. The remaining requirements follow the list above. The notice prints "2 to 5. As nos. 2 to 5 above", although only nos. 2 to 4 appear in that list. Experience of digital archiving, scanning and digital photography. Formal training in digital humanities. Check the official notification for the discipline-specific eligibility of each post.

rows.event: Last date for submission of forms

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Interview: the date, time and place will be notified only on the website carrying this notice, at least seven days in advance. A typing test may be held. There may also be a test in Avro keyboard operation and text correction.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: Appointments will be for one year with possibility of limited renewal. The project is run entirely from donations and can continue only as long as funding is available from voluntary donors. Appointments may therefore have to be terminated at any time before the completion of one year.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for JU Project Fellow Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Collect the application form from the university Information Office. Fill in the form. Submit the completed form with your relevant documents at the office of the School of Cultural Texts and Records, Fifth floor, Rabindra Bhaban, JU Main Campus.

faq.question: Q1. Can I apply if my Master's degree is not in Humanities or computing?
faq.answer: Yes, for the two general posts. Holders of a Master's degree in other disciplines may be considered if found suitable in other respects, but the 55% minimum still applies.

faq.question: Q2. Which degree is needed for the third post?
faq.answer: The third post requires a Master's degree in Sanskrit with minimum 55% marks.

faq.question: Q3. What computer experience is required?
faq.answer: Candidates need experience of computer operation in projects involving textual computing, computational linguistics, natural language processing or another relevant field.

faq.question: Q4. Which keyboard software should I know?
faq.answer: The notice requires skill in operating the Bengali keyboard with Avro software.

faq.question: Q5. Will I get an individual interview letter?
faq.answer: No. The notice says no notice will be sent individually to candidates, so the website announcement is the only intimation.

faq.question: Q6. Where do I get the application form?
faq.answer: Forms are available at the university Information Office.

faq.question: Q7. Can the appointment end before one year?
faq.answer: Yes. Because funding depends on voluntary donors, an appointment may have to be terminated before the year is complete.
